stem: A client is unable to get out of bed while the linens are changed. Which bed-making technique is appropriate?

options.A: Use an occupied-bed technique, turning the client safely from side to side while changing one half of the bed at a time and maintaining coverage and privacy.
options.B: Postpone linen changes until the client can stand independently even when the linens are soiled.
options.C: Remove all linens first and leave the client uncovered while the replacement linens are prepared.
options.D: Have the immobile client stand briefly at the bedside so the linens can be changed more quickly.

rationale: NCBI Nursing Assistant guidance provides an occupied-bed checklist for clients who remain in bed. The technique uses safe side-to-side rolling while soiled linens are rolled inward and clean linens are placed on one side and then pulled through after the client is turned. Privacy, coverage, safe handling, and post-procedure safety are maintained throughout. A is therefore correct; B through D unnecessarily delay care or create privacy and fall/injury risks.
educational_objective: Use the occupied-bed technique to change linens safely for a client who must remain in bed while preserving privacy, comfort, and safe repositioning.

source_original.stem: A nurse needs to change the bed linens for a client who is unable to get out of bed. The nurse should use which technique?

options.A: Use occupied-bed technique, turning the client safely from side to side
options.B: Postpone linen changes until the client can get out of bed independently
options.C: Remove all linens first and leave the client uncovered during replacement
options.D: Ask the immobile client to stand briefly while the linens are replaced

source_original.rationale: For a client unable to get out of bed, the nurse uses the occupied bed-making technique, working from one side of the bed to the other, safely rolling the client (with assistance as needed) while maintaining the client's privacy, safety, comfort, and proper body mechanics for the nurse throughout the process.
source_original.source_detail: Occupied-bed checklist and safe linen-change technique for a client who remains in bed; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Retained the occupied-bed technique, added privacy/coverage and one-half-at-a-time workflow directly from the checklist, removed vague body-mechanics claims not needed for the construct, and preserved easy difficulty.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Basic hygiene/environmental care — occupied bed making
audit_findings.source_authority: NCBI Nursing Assistant; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.currentness: Current NCBI checklist remains available and directly supports the procedure.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Section 3.6 directly supports side-to-side rolling, staged linen changes, coverage, privacy, and final safety checks.

distractor_audit.B: Soiled linens should not be postponed solely because the client cannot stand.
distractor_audit.C: Checklist keeps the resident covered and does not require full exposure.
distractor_audit.D: An immobile client should not be made to stand just to change linens.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A describes the established occupied-bed technique.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are linen-change strategies; no second safe method is offered.
audit_findings.blueprint: Basic Care and Comfort is appropriate for hygiene, linen, positioning, and comfort care.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read the occupied-bed checklist, checked privacy and side-to-side workflow, challenged whether assistance should be universalized, retained only 'safely' rather than a fixed assistance requirement, and confirmed A remained uniquely correct.
